style: Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G and its quantities in blue, dual grid G-tilde and its quantities in orange, exact/topological items in dark grey, approximate/material items in green, failure or warning items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

figures.caption: Figure 6.1: Domain-edge boundary alignment in GridFIT3D. Top: in legacy mode (boundary_at_domain_edge=False), the field array has Nx = N samples, so node x_N = x_max has no stored electric edge; a high PEC wall sits one cell inside at x_{N−1} = x_max − Δx (shrinking the cavity to (N−1)Δx) and a high PMC wall zeros H at x_{N−1/2} (shifted by Δx/2). Bottom: with boundary_at_domain_edge=True (default), one ghost layer gives solver.Nx = Nx + 1 samples, placing PEC and PMC boundaries on the exact domain edge x_max to second order O(Δx²).
figures.visual_intent: Scripted Matplotlib recipe (two horizontal 1D/2D staggered-grid strips stacked vertically for N = 5 cells spanning [x_0 = x_min, x_N = x_max], 13.76 × 7.68 in at 200 dpi). TOP PANEL (heading 'Legacy mode: boundary_at_domain_edge=False  (Nx = N)', line 1100): draw N = 5 primary cells of width Δx with primary nodes at x_0 = x_min, x_1, ..., x_{N−1}, x_N = x_max (vertical blue lines) and dual midpoints at x_{1/2}, ..., x_{N−1/2} (vertical dashed orange lines). Plot stored tangential E samples (filled blue circles) at x_0, x_1, ..., x_{N−1}, and an open red circle with a cross at x_N = x_max labelled 'no E sample stored at x_N = x_max'. Plot tangential H samples (filled orange squares) at x_{1/2}, ..., x_{N−1/2}. Mark a red vertical wall at x_{N−1} = x_max − Δx labelled 'high PEC wall at x_{N−1}: effective length (N−1)Δx,  O(Δx/L) ~ 5% frequency shift', and a second red marker at x_{N−1/2} labelled 'high PMC wall zeros H at x_{N−1/2} (shifted by Δx/2)'. BOTTOM PANEL (heading 'Exact Domain-Edge Mode: boundary_at_domain_edge=True (default, solver.Nx = Nx + 1)', lines 1101–1103): draw the same N primary cells [x_0, x_N] plus one dashed grey ghost cell [x_N, x_N + Δx] beyond x_max shaded light grey and labelled 'ghost layer outside domain: μ⁻¹ = 0'. Plot stored tangential E samples (filled blue circles) at all N + 1 nodes x_0 = x_min through x_N = x_max. Highlight the truncated boundary dual cell Ã_k ending at x_N = x_max in light orange. At x_0 = x_min and x_N = x_max draw thick green boundary bars with two callouts: 'PEC wall: zeros tangential E on node 0 (x_min) and node N (x_max)' and 'PMC wall: dual face Ã_k truncated at x_max + ghost μ⁻¹ = 0  ⇒  n̂ × H = 0 on x_max to O(Δx²)'.

figures.caption: Figure 6.3: Nonuniform Cartesian meshing and automatic STL feature snapping in GridFIT3D. Left: explicit graded node array x_nodes combining a uniform fine core x_fine in [−5 mm, 5 mm] with geometric outer wings x_left and x_right out to ±50 mm, keeping adjacent cell ratios within 1/grading ≤ Δx_{i+1}/Δx_i ≤ 1.2–1.3. Right: automatic feature snapping (use_mesh_refinement=True, snap_tol=1e-4) aligns grid planes with STL feature planes via refinement_method='insert' or 'stretch'.
figures.visual_intent: Scripted Matplotlib recipe (two panels side by side, 13.76 × 7.68 in at 200 dpi). LEFT PANEL (lines 1174–1178, 1206): execute the exact code from lines 1175–1178: x_fine = np.linspace(-5e-3, 5e-3, 41); x_left = np.geomspace(-50e-3, -5e-3, 25)[:-1]; x_right = np.geomspace(5e-3, 50e-3, 25)[1:]; x_nodes = np.concatenate([x_left, x_fine, x_right]). Top sub-axes: draw vertical blue ticks at every node in x_nodes (in mm from -50 to +50), shading [-5, 5] mm in light blue ('x_fine: 41 nodes') and [-50, -5] mm / [5, 50] mm in light orange ('x_left, x_right: geomspace'). Bottom sub-axes: plot cell size Δx_i = np.diff(x_nodes)*1e3 [mm] versus cell midpoint (blue curve with dots) and on a twin orange axis plot the adjacent ratio max(Δx_{i+1}/Δx_i, Δx_i/Δx_{i+1}), with a green shaded band showing 'smooth grading: 1/grading ≤ Δx_{i+1}/Δx_i ≤ 1.2–1.3' and grey annotation 'global CFL Δt governed by min(Δx_i, Δy_j, Δz_k)'. RIGHT PANEL (lines 1191–1200): draw an axisymmetric cavity STL profile at the top with two vertical dashed green lines extending down from the iris corners labelled 'STL feature planes (snap_tol=1e-4)'. Below the cavity profile, draw three horizontal z-grid strips stacked vertically: Strip 1 'Uniform grid (use_mesh_refinement=False)' showing blue grid lines missing both dashed green feature planes (marked with red crosses); Strip 2 'refinement_method="insert"' showing extra grid planes inserted exactly on the green feature planes (highlighted in green); Strip 3 'refinement_method="stretch"' showing the nearest existing grid nodes shifted onto the green feature planes with smoothly adjusted neighbour spacing.

figures.caption: Figure 6.4: Conformal Dey–Mittra PEC cut cells and thin conducting sheets. Left: on a cell cut by a PEC boundary, Faraday's law uses the vacuum-open edge lengths l_k ∈ [0, |L_k|] in D_s = diag(l_k) and open face area S_f ∈ [0, |A_f|] in iA_f = 1/S_f. Centre: an unstable small cut face (S_f < 0.5 A_stab, with A_stab = max_i(l_i h_i)/2) redistributes its flux with weights (2, −1) to its first and second in-plane neighbours via the symmetric positive semi-definite operator G = Tᵀ diag(1/Â) T. Right: an infinitely thin conducting Sheet on a grid plane uses a quasi-static Meixner r^{−1/2} singularity correction on primary faces outside its sharp edge.

Draw the vacuum-open portions of the cut edges as thick blue segments labelled 'l_k ∈ [0, |L_k|]' and 'D_s = diag(l_k)', an enclosed edge inside PEC in red dashed labelled 'l_k = 0  ⇒  ieps = 0', and shade the vacuum aperture of the face in light blue labelled 'S_f ∈ [0, |A_f|],  iA_f = 1/S_f'. CENTRE PANEL (heading '2. (2, −1) small-face stabilization', lines 1219–1224): draw a 3 × 2 Cartesian grid patch cut by a curved PEC wall so that column 0 has a tiny sliver open area S_u (shaded light red, labelled 'unstable face u: S_u < 0.5 A_stab') while columns 1 and 2 in the same row are stable in-plane neighbours along the longest open edge (shaded light green, labelled 'neighbour 1 (n_1)' and 'neighbour 2 (n_2)'). Draw two curved green arrows from face u to n_1 and n_2 with badge labels '+2' and '−1' (and note 'weight 1 if only one neighbour'). Below the grid, typeset the exact equations from lines 1221–1224: 'A_stab = max_i(l_i h_i)/2,  MERGE_THRESHOLD = 0.5', 'Â_n = A_n + Σ_u T_{nu} A_u', and 'G = Tᵀ diag(1/Â) T  (symmetric positive semi-definite)', with green badge 'stable Δt = 0.85–0.97 of Yee limit (studies/conformal-pec-mask/)'. RIGHT PANEL (heading '3. Thin Sheet & Meixner edge correction', lines 1226–1249): draw a 2D (x, z) grid cross-section with a horizontal zero-thickness metallic sheet (thick dark-grey bar at z = 1.5 mm, x ≤ 0, labelled 'Sheet(size=(30e-3, 40e-3, 0.0))'). Highlight the primary face immediately outside the sharp edge (x ∈ [0, Δx]) in light orange, and plot above it the exact analytical curve r^{−1/2} versus distance r from the edge (orange curve), labelled 'sheet_edge_correction=True: quasi-static Meixner r^{−1/2} correction'.

figures.caption: Figure 6.5: Kottke dielectric subpixel smoothing in GridFIT3D. Left: across a curved dielectric interface with normal n̂ cutting dual cell Ṽ_k, tangential E_∥ and normal D_⊥ = ε E_⊥ are continuous; Wakis evaluates volume averages ⟨f⟩ over Ṽ_k with m³ = 4³ = 64 subcell quadrature samples (conformal_subsamples=4). Centre: conformal='all' uses the diagonal entries T_{xx}, T_{yy}, T_{zz} with zero runtime overhead. Right: conformal='tensor' applies the full symmetric tensor T via an 8-octant gather/scatter operator solver.ieps_tensor to restore O(h²) accuracy on tilted high-contrast interfaces.
figures.visual_intent: Three panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (heading '1. Cut dual cell Ṽ_k & Kottke tensor'): a square dual cell Ṽ_k (orange dashed border) cut by a tilted curved interface between dielectric 'ε₁' (white) and dielectric 'ε₂' (light green), with unit normal arrow 'n̂', tangential vector arrow 'E_∥ continuous', and normal vector arrow 'D_⊥ = ε E_⊥ continuous'. Overlay a 4 × 4 grid of small orange dots inside Ṽ_k labelled 'conformal_subsamples=4 (4³ = 64 quadrature points in 3D)'. Below the cell, the exact equation 'T = ⟨ε⁻¹⟩ n̂ n̂ᵀ + ⟨ε⟩⁻¹ (I − n̂ n̂ᵀ)'. CENTRE PANEL (blue border, heading '2. Diagonal Kottke: conformal="all"'): a primary cell with three uncoupled edge arrows E_x, E_y, E_z along the coordinate axes, and formula 'solver.ieps uses diagonal entries: T_{cc} = n_c² ⟨ε⁻¹⟩ + (1 − n_c²) ⟨ε⟩⁻¹'. At the bottom, two green badges: 'O(h²) for axis-aligned or moderate contrast' and 'zero runtime overhead after setup'. RIGHT PANEL (green border, heading '3. Full Symmetric Tensor: conformal="tensor"'): a 3D primary cube subdivided into 8 octants around a 45°-tilted interface, with one octant highlighted showing its three adjacent edge components (E_x, E_y, E_z in blue) gathered into the octant, coupled by off-diagonal arrows 'T_{ab} = (⟨ε⁻¹⟩ − ⟨ε⟩⁻¹) n_a n_b  (a ≠ b)', and scattered back by the transpose ('solver.ieps_tensor'). At the bottom, two badges: green badge '8-octant SPD gather/scatter: O(h²) on 45° high-contrast interfaces' and grey badge '+15% step cost on GPU, +5% on CPU'.

figures.caption: Figure 6.6: Exploiting mirror symmetry planes with boundary_at_domain_edge=True. Left: a PEC symmetry plane ('pec', n̂ × E = 0, n̂ · B = 0) models fields whose tangential E is odd under reflection (such as a z-directed dipole cut by z = 0). Centre: a PMC symmetry plane ('pmc', n̂ × H = 0, n̂ · D = 0) models fields whose tangential E is even under reflection (such as an on-axis current J_z). Right: placing xmin=0, ymin=0 with bc_low=['pmc', 'pmc', 'pec'] simulates one quadrant of an axisymmetric cavity and on-axis beam, cutting cell count and runtime by 4×.
figures.visual_intent: Three panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (blue border, heading 'PEC symmetry plane ("pec")'): a horizontal mirror plane labelled 'z = 0: n̂ × E = 0,  n̂ · B = 0' cutting a vertical z-directed dipole arrow at the origin. On the left and right of the dipole, draw tangential electric field arrows above z = 0 pointing outward and mirrored arrows below z = 0 pointing inward, labelled 'tangential E is odd (antisymmetric)'. Bottom note: 'currents normal to plane, or antisymmetric tangential currents'. CENTRE PANEL (orange border, heading 'PMC symmetry plane ("pmc")'): a vertical mirror plane labelled 'x = 0: n̂ × H = 0,  n̂ · D = 0' with an on-axis current arrow 'J_z(0, 0, z)' running along the plane. On both sides of x = 0, draw tangential electric field arrows pointing in the same vertical direction, labelled 'tangential E is even (symmetric)'. Bottom note: 'currents tangential to plane and symmetric'. RIGHT PANEL (green border, heading 'Quarter-domain wakefield example (4× reduction)'): a circular axisymmetric cavity cross-section in the (x, y) plane centred at (0, 0) with an on-axis beam dot at the origin labelled 'J_z(0, 0, z)', radial blue arrows 'E_ρ (tangential to x = 0, y = 0)', and dashed orange circular loops 'H_φ (normal to x = 0, y = 0  ⇒  n̂ × H = 0)'. Shade the first quadrant (x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0) brightly with a blue grid and fade the other three quadrants in light grey. Label the two symmetry axes 'xmin = 0.0: bc_low[0] = "pmc"' and 'ymin = 0.0: bc_low[1] = "pmc"', with a green badge 'boundary_at_domain_edge=True: 4× fewer cells (15×15×61 vs 30×30×61)'.
